# Host support

sharpen keeps its gate policy in stdlib Python that every host runs the same
way, and adds native enhancements where a host offers them. This page says
what each host actually does, so nobody has to infer it from the code.

## What every native host gets

On Claude Code, Codex and pi:

- Opening a PR is blocked until the gate cycle is complete, on every path
  `plugins/sdlc/scripts/pr_paths.py` recognizes: `gh pr create`/`gh pr new`,
  `gh api` POSTs to `.../pulls` and the graphql `createPullRequest` mutation,
  `glab mr create`, `hub pull-request`, `git push -o merge_request.create`,
  Claude Code's `Monitor` tool, and MCP `create_pull_request`/
  `create_merge_request` tools.
- A git pre-push hook warns (or, with `git config sharpen.prePush block`,
  refuses) when a pushed branch's gates are missing or stale. It is the floor
  under the PR hook for what no tool hook reads: scripts, aliases, `curl`, a
  push followed by the web UI. Auto-init installs it when it arms a cycle, and
  every `/sdlc:gate` refreshes it.
- The first commit to a feature branch arms a gate cycle (`small-medium`, or
  `tiny` for a docs-only diff).
- Gates 2 to 6 record from the receipt each grumpy pass leaves, through
  `record-gate.py --verify <pass>`. On Claude Code and pi a host event also
  sweeps receipts at the end of every turn, so recording is automatic. On
  Codex, run `--verify` after each pass until its `Stop` hook is confirmed.

The tier alone decides which gates a cycle requires, on every host. A host
that lacks grumpy still gets a `small-medium` cycle, and the arming message
names the missing passes, so the choice to install grumpy or re-init as
`tiny` stays with a person.

## Which host is running

The session-start adapter (`plugins/sdlc/scripts/session-start.py`) names the
host and writes `.sharpen/data/capabilities.<host>.json`:

1. `SHARPEN_HOST`, when an adapter sets it. The pi extension exports
   `SHARPEN_HOST=pi`.
2. `CLAUDECODE=1`, which Claude Code exports to every process it starts:
   `claude-code`.
3. Otherwise `unknown`. Codex has no confirmed signal yet, so it reports
   `unknown` and is told to run `--verify` by hand. To name a host yourself,
   export `SHARPEN_HOST` before starting it.

The `SHARPEN_HOST` values that change behavior are `claude-code`, `codex` and
`pi`. Any other well-formed value (letters, digits, `.` and `-`, up to 64
characters, case folded to lowercase) is accepted as a label: it
gets its own manifest file and manual recording, like `unknown`. A malformed
value is treated as `unknown`. Don't use `claude`: it writes
`capabilities.claude.json`, the pre-4.15 file name that Claude Code still
reads as a fallback.

One file per host means a Claude Code session and a pi or Codex session in
the same repo no longer overwrite each other. Besides the v1 fields, the
manifest records:

- `x-recording`: `automatic` when a host event sweeps receipts, else `manual`.
  A declaration for other readers: auto-init takes the recording mode from the
  host table above, so the two can't disagree.
- `x-receipts`: whether the installed grumpy writes receipts (grumpy 2.9.0 or
  later ships `scripts/receipt.py`). With an older grumpy on Claude Code,
  auto-init arms an event-only cycle, which Claude Code's `Skill` event can
  stamp, instead of a receipt-backed one that could never complete. No other
  host has that event, so there the cycle stays receipt-backed and the arming
  message says gates 2-6 can't record until grumpy is upgraded (or, as a last
  resort, `--attest` per gate). `SDLC_GATE_EVIDENCE=events` still forces
  event-only cycles by hand.
- `x-source`: `session-start` from 4.15 on. A manifest without it (a pre-4.15
  `capabilities.claude.json`) predates the `simplify` capability, so auto-init
  treats its silence on `simplify` as unknown rather than reporting it missing.

## Plugin roots in skill text

Every plugin path in a command or SKILL.md is spelled with the plugin's own
variable first, falling back to the braced shared name:

| Plugin | Spelling |
|---|---|
| sdlc | `${SDLC_PLUGIN_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}}` |
| grumpy | `${GRUMPY_PLUGIN_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}}` |
| sdlc-guardrails | `${GUARDRAILS_PLUGIN_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}}` |

Why this shape:

- **Claude Code** substitutes the braced `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in a plugin's
  command and skill text when it loads it, and does not export the variable
  to the agent's shell. An unbraced `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is therefore an
  empty shell variable there. Checked against the Claude Code 2.1.42 binary.
- **pi** does no substitution and runs every plugin in one process. A single
  shared `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` would point every plugin at whichever extension
  set it last, so each extension exports its own variable and none sets the
  shared one.
- **Codex** fills in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in hook commands (verified live).
  Whether it does the same in skill text is unverified.

`scripts/check-marketplace.py` fails on an unbraced `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` or a
plugin path that doesn't lead with its own plugin's variable. Hook commands in
`hooks/hooks.json` keep the plain `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"`, which every native
host fills in.

## Instructions only: Gemini, Cursor, Copilot and `npx skills add`

These hosts read the generated `skills/*/SKILL.md` files and nothing else. No
hook runs, so nothing blocks an ungated PR, nothing arms a cycle, and nothing
records a gate. `npx skills add` copies the SKILL.md files without the
`scripts/` they call, so any step that runs a sharpen script fails there
(sharpen#46). Treat these as a way to read the workflow, not to enforce it;
enforcement needs the Claude Code or Codex plugin install, or `pi install`.

## Where sharpen writes

Plans, specs, review reports and receipts go under `.sharpen/sdlc/<branch>/`
and `.sharpen/grumpy/<branch>/` (sdlc 4.21, grumpy 2.15), next to the gate
state in `.sharpen/data/`. They used to go under `.claude/`, which Claude Code
treats as its own configuration. The old folders are still read, never
written: a receipt counts by whichever copy is newer, a plan or `fix.md` found
only there is copied into `.sharpen/` before a pass appends to it, and other
files are read from there when the new copy is missing.

What is known about writing under `.claude/`, per host:

- **Claude Code, checked in the 2.1.42 binary:** `.claude` is on its list of
  sensitive directory names, and a file-tool write there gets a safety check
  marked not classifier-approvable, with the `restrictedMode` circuit breaker.
  `.claude/commands`, `.claude/agents`, `.claude/skills` and the settings
  files are treated as config outright.
- **Claude Code, inferred, not run:** interactively that check is a prompt a
  person can accept; headless (`claude -p`), nobody can, so the write is
  refused. The review benchmark saw exactly that: the pass printed its report
  instead of saving it. The check covers the file tools, not a shell, which is
  why receipts written by `receipt.py` and worktrees made by `git worktree add`
  were not affected. Whether `--dangerously-skip-permissions` lifts it is
  unverified.
- **Codex and pi:** no rule about `.claude/` was found in either; unverified.
  Check 5 below and the one under [Verifying pi](#verifying-pi) settle it.

## Verifying Codex

Five Codex behaviours are marked unverified until someone runs them in a
throwaway repo, with sharpen installed in Codex:

1. **Plugin root in skill text.** Run `/sdlc:gate --status`, or any skill step
   that shells out to `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/record-gate.py" --status`.
   It passes if the script runs. It fails if Codex tries `/scripts/record-gate.py`.
2. **`Stop` hook.** On a feature branch, commit once so auto-init arms a cycle,
   run `/grumpy:review` to completion, and end the turn without `--verify`. Then
   run `python3 <sdlc root>/scripts/record-gate.py --status`. It passes if
   `grumpy-review` is recorded.
3. **Host signal.** Inside Codex, run
   `env | grep -iE '^(codex|openai)' | cut -d= -f1`. The variable names alone,
   no values, say what `detect_host()` can key on.
4. **Model per role.** Codex can't choose a model per subagent, so grumpy's
   passes run on the session's model, and the `codex` column of grumpy's
   `models.yaml` only says which model to start the session on. Its ids are
   unverified: run `python3 scripts/bench-grumpy.py run --host codex --model
   <id>` for each and compare.
5. **Writes under `.claude/`.** Ask Codex to save a one-line file to
   `.claude/grumpy/probe.md` with its file-editing tool (not a shell
   command), non-interactively (`codex exec`). It passes if the file exists
   afterwards. Nothing depends on it any more, but a failure would mean a
   Codex user on an older grumpy loses reports the same way headless Claude
   Code did.

When one of the first three is confirmed, update `HOSTS` in `hosts.py` (and `detect_host()` for
the third), regenerate this page, and the `unverified` marks go with it.

## Verifying pi

One pi behaviour is unverified:

1. **Writes under `.claude/`.** In a pi session with sharpen installed, ask pi
   to save a one-line file to `.claude/grumpy/probe.md` with its write tool,
   once interactively and once headless. It passes if the file exists both
   times. As with Codex check 4, nothing depends on it since grumpy 2.15; it
   says whether an older grumpy works there.
